chunks: 2674 - And it was narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام:
That he was asked, “What is the difference between the tent and the shade of the litter?” He said:
“One should not seek shade in the litter, and the difference between them is that a woman menstruates in the month of Ramaḍān, so she makes up the fasting and does not make up the salat (prayer).”
He said, “You have spoken the truth; may I be your ransom.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: ritual prayer that is not made up in this case
key_terms.الصِّيَامَ: fasting that must be made up
key_terms.الْمَحْمِلِ: a litter or riding carriage with covering

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a tent and the shade of a litter for a muhrim in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal distinction related to the muhrim and the use of shade, clarifying that seeking shade in the maḥmil is not appropriate. The Imam عليه السلام explains the difference by analogy to a menstruating woman in Ramaḍān, who must make up the sawm (fasting) but not the salat (prayer), indicating that similar rulings may differ in legal consequence despite apparent similarity.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2674 - It was narrated from Al-Husayn ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far the Second (as): "What is the difference between a tent (fusṭāṭ) and the shade of a litter (maḥmil)?"

Imam (as) said: "One should not seek shade in the maḥmil. The difference between them is like the case of a woman who menstruates during Month of Ramadan; she makes up the fasts but does not make up the prayers."
I replied: "You have spoken the truth, may I be your ransom."
